record.paper_title: Packings and coverings of groups: some results and open problems
record.original_question: Let G be an infinite group with identity element e. A subset A of G is 2-thin if |gA ∩ A| <= 2 for every g in G with g != e. A subset A is self-linked if pack(A) = 1, equivalently if gA ∩ A is nonempty for every g in G, or equivalently if G = AA^{-1}. Does every infinite group G contain a subset A that is both 2-thin and self-linked?

evidence.quote: For a natural number k, it is more convenient to say that a subset A of G is k-thin if |gA ∩ A| 6 k for every g ∈ G, g 6= e.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be an infinite group with identity element $e$. For a subset $A \subseteq G$:

- $A$ is called $2$-thin if $|gA \cap A| \le 2$ for every $g \in G$ with $g \ne e$.
- $A$ is called self-linked if $gA \cap A \ne \emptyset$ for every $g \in G$; equivalently, $G = AA^{-1}$.

Question: Does every infinite group $G$ contain a subset $A \subseteq G$ that is simultaneously $2$-thin and self-linked?
artifact.category_tag: Combinatorics of infinite groups / thin subsets
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is recorded as an open question in the literature on combinatorial size and packing/covering of subsets of groups. Partial results are known: every countable group admits a thin subset $A$ with $G = AA^{-1}$, and the statement is true under additional hypotheses such as $G$ being abelian. No proof or counterexample for arbitrary infinite groups appears to be available.

status_evidence.title: Thin systems of generators of groups
status_evidence.snippet: Every countable group G has a thin subset A such that G = AA^{-1}.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist (countable groups admit thin A with G=AA^{-1}); the general 2-thin self-linked question is recorded as a problem.

status_evidence.title: On Factoring Groups into Thin Subsets
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of thin subsets of groups and related open problems following Protasov.
status_evidence.claim: The framework of k-thin subsets and self-linked subsets is an active research area with several open problems.
